To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the application of newly acquired leadership and management skills is influenced by a number of factors, both internal and external, and that these factors can be grouped into two categories, namely, facilitators and inhibitors.
the application of leadership practices in the workplace is a complex process and that it is not only dependent on the individual, but also on the environment.
leadership and management development programmes can be effective if the right people attend the programmes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the transfer of training and the factors that influence it.
the transfer of training of newly acquired leadership knowledge and skills back into the workplace.

the extent to which delegates who successfully complete the leadership and management development programmes at the University of the Witwatersrand apply newly acquired knowledge in their respective work contexts and the factors that influence this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the application of newly acquired knowledge and skill is a very complicated process, and is dependent on many factors.
the transfer of training is a complex and multi-layered phenomenon.
the transfer of learning from a structured leadership and development programme is a complex phenomenon.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the transfer of training of the newly acquired leadership practices was not always as intended and/or as planned.

leadership and management interventions, such as the one in this study, are not only about the acquisition of new knowledge and skills but also about the implementation and application of these new knowledge and skills back at the workplace.
leadership and management development programmes should be designed to be more inclusive and to address the needs of the line managers and the organisational culture.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transfer of training is not an automatic process and is dependent on a variety of factors.
the transfer of training is a complex phenomenon and is influenced by many factors, which are not always within the control of the individual.

leadership development programmes can be effective in changing and enhancing leadership practices in the workplace, provided that the programme is well designed and the environment is conducive to the implementation of the newly acquired skills and practices.
